story_type: helicopter bucket drops on a wildfire
hook: A Chinook drops tons of water right onto a Maui wildfire.
narration: This bucket is opening right over the flames.
It was August ninth, 2023, and wildfires were burning across Maui.
Two Hawaii Army National Guard Chinooks were sent to the fire lines in Upcountry Maui.
Under each one hung a giant bucket on a long line. The crew dips it into a reservoir, and it fills in seconds.
Then they fly it back to the fire, with the full load swinging below the helicopter.
The pilots cannot see the bucket under them. A crew member watching through a hatch in the floor calls the drop. [short pause]
Below them, the fire was still moving through dry grass.
So the crews flew the same loop again and again, from the water to the flames and back.
outcome: In five hours, the two crews made fifty eight drops and poured more than one hundred thousand gallons of water on the fires.
title: Chinook bucket drops on a Maui wildfire
description:
On Aug. 9, 2023, two Hawaii Army National Guard CH-47 Chinook crews fought wildfires in Upcountry Maui, Hawaii, making 58 bucket drops of more than 100,000 gallons of water in five hours.

Footage: U.S. National Guard video by Air Force Master Sgt. Andrew Jackson, State of Hawaii Department of Defense, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/893267/hawaii-army-national-guard-provides-water-bucket-support-wildfires-maui-part-2
